reason: Defs/Part9.lean:24 adds finiteness of the positive-mass support to the canonical claim's arbitrary atomic design with positive target exposure probabilities. This excludes all infinite positive-support designs, including ones satisfying the author's usual existence and integrability conditions. On its finite-support domain, the statement correctly renders every clause (a)-(d): the exposure probability is the support sum, EPOs are normalized conditional atomic means, AEPOs are their finite averages, and EED/AEED satisfy Equations (7)-(8). Both target exposure positivities are the printed Condition 4.1; no stability of responses within an exposure is imposed. An arbitrary assignment type is a harmless abstraction of the feasible-assignment labels, and the implicit power-set atomic law supplies the relevant ordinary conditional expectation. All SAP definitions are the actual weighted sums and contrasts, not placeholders. The added finite-support hypothesis is substantive but is disclosed exactly at Challenge/Part1.lean:80-82. The compiled scratch/Check.lean instance has feasible set Nat, masses 1/3 at 0,1,2 and zero elsewhere, N=1, exposure 0 at assignment 0 and 1 elsewhere, response y(z)=z, and targets 1 and 0. It supplies every hypothesis, proves response instability within exposure 1, and independently computes both exposure-one mean formulas as 3/2. Consequently the theorem is nonvacuous, uses no junk values, and faithfully states the finite-support restriction of the canonical claim.
